description: Atomic mass and Q-value tables by Hecke level k=3,4,5 with explicit error bounds. Each nucleus shows B(k=3), B(k=4), B(k=5) vs AME2020, with truncation, parametric (δq), and CODATA input uncertainties. Q-values computed by both NF trace ratio and BW difference methods.

unified_path.description: Unified iterative LP-dual accumulator — ONE consistent algorithm, no special cases, runs from A = 1 over EVERY partition λ ⊢ k for k = 2, …, K_PARTITION_MAX.  Per-step contribution per partition: ΔB_λ(step) = m_e · H_q(λ) · y_λ · (ln|Tr M_λ^(0..step)| − ln|Tr M_λ^(0..step-1)|).  Telescopes to B_λ = m_e · H_q(λ) · y_λ · (ln|Tr M_λ^(0..A)| − ln d_λ).  Total = Σ_λ B_λ.  References: prop:unified-iterative-correction, prop:bw-coefficient-shadow-price.
unified_path.energy_scale_derivation: Per-partition: C_λ = m_e × H_q(λ) (q-hook product).  For (2,2): H_q = [3]·[2]² → C_(2,2) ≈ 6.29 MeV (matches empirical Δ_W).
unified_path.lp_dual_shadow_price: y_λ = w_λ/d_λ − 1/[k]_q! where w_λ is the Wedderburn weight, d_λ the classical dimension, and 1/[k]_q! the LP normalisation dual variable (smallest w_λ/d_λ across partitions of k, attained by the trivial sym/alt 1-dim reps).  1-dim reps therefore have y_λ = 0 and contribute nothing; only mixing partitions feed the unified accumulator.
